_provenance: TRANSCRIBED FROM SPEC TEST SOURCE -- see README.md. The payloads are the specification's, taken from sdks/typescript/packages/proto/__tests__/usage-roundtrip.test.ts at commit e42bdbe. The JSON encoding is ours: the originals are TypeScript object literals, so this file is a transcription and carries our transcription bugs, not the spec's authority. Licence: LICENSE.ag-ui-typescript.
_why_here: null-omission.json covers almost every event type but carries no usage entries at all, and RUN_FINISHED.usage is where kobold_proto::Usage breaks -- camelCase, an array, every count optional, and two counts we have no field for. These are the cases that pin the fold from Vec<TokenUsage> to Kobold's flat gauge.

cases.name: run_finished_with_a_single_fully_populated_usage_entry
cases.note: Every field set. reasoningTokens and cachedInputTokens have no counterpart in kobold_proto::Usage.

cases.name: run_finished_with_multiple_usage_entries_per_model
cases.note: The reason usage is an array. A fold that reads entry [0] and stops loses the second model entirely, and nothing about the shape makes that visible.

cases.name: run_finished_with_usage_alongside_outcome_and_result
cases.note: A totalTokens with no inputTokens or outputTokens. Any fold that computes a total by summing input and output reports zero here.

cases.name: run_error_with_partial_usage
cases.note: Usage on a FAILED run, and an inputTokens with no total. A run that died after billing still costs money, and Kobold's Update::Failed carries no usage at all today.

cases.name: legacy_run_finished_with_no_usage_key_at_all
cases.note: Absent, not zero. The distinction kobold_proto::Usage's own doc comment exists to protect.
